group.passage:
Charles Darwin was left confused for the rest of his life by a Halloween mystery. On October 31, 1832, thousands of tiny red spiders landed from nowhere on his ship, the HMS Beagle. This phenomenon sparked shock, curiosity, and quite an itching. Young Darwin noted that the winds were calm, these small aviators did not have wings, and the migrating birds did not dump them as they flew by. So how did they travel 60 miles across the ocean from the Argentine coast? This evolutionist said the invasion was “inexplicable.” And it really was, until now.
It was far from a Halloween prank. Scientists now understand that the atmosphere is positively charged and the Earth is negatively charged. Like magnets, similar charges repel each other and opposite charges attract. It is this interaction that creates the electric field, which is always active and especially strong during thunderstorms. Using this electric field, spiders are able to defy gravity with an extraordinary behavior known as “ballooning” and embark on amazing flight journeys.
The starting point for a spider to soar is high up in a tree branch, leaf or fence, where the Earth’s electric field is strongest. Here, the spider first secures itself with anchor silk, raises its front legs, and then uses tiny sensory hairs to detect wind and electrical conditions, as if turning itself into a living weather station. This careful assessment of the environment determines the best moment to launch.
Once it senses that conditions are favorable, the spider stands on tiptoe with its hind legs, raises its abdomen, and releases its silk threads into the air. Instead of tangling, these strands, carrying static electricity, repel away from one another. This reaction, combined with the wind, provides the spider with the lift it needs to disconnect from its anchor and rise into the air. During flight, it may adjust its legs to maintain balance and control its speed. This sophisticated interaction with the environment allows the spider to set out on cross-continental journeys to seek new territories or avoid predators.

figures.label: 第3題選項 (A)–(D)
figures.caption: 第3題選項 (A)–(D)：四張蜘蛛放絲的灰階插圖
figures.description: 四個選項皆為灰階插圖，排成 2×2（上排 (A)(B)、下排 (C)(D)），每張圖中一隻蜘蛛頭朝左，從腹部末端向右上方放出蛛絲。(A)：蜘蛛站在一根長著幾片葉子的樹枝上，兩隻前腳向上舉起，身體大致水平；蛛絲先是一條細線斜向右上，到末端在空中糾纏成一大團捲曲、打結的亂絲。(B)：蜘蛛站在一根長著幾片葉子的樹枝上，以腳尖站立、腹部向上翹起；蛛絲從腹部末端斜向右上，末端分成許多條筆直的細絲呈扇形散開，彼此分離、沒有糾纏。(C)：蜘蛛伏在平坦的地面上（地面畫成帶小石子的沙土），身體貼近地面；蛛絲斜向右上，末端分成許多條弧形細絲向外散開，絲線彼此交叉。(D)：蜘蛛伏在平坦的地面上（帶小石子的沙土），身體貼近地面；蛛絲斜向右上，末端是幾條細長的波浪狀絲線，彼此靠攏、互相纏繞成一束向上飄。
rows: 末端糾纏成一團捲曲亂絲
多條筆直細絲呈扇形散開、彼此分離
多條弧形細絲向外散開、互相交叉
幾條波浪狀細絲靠攏纏繞成一束

questions.stem: What can be assumed from the evolutionist’s description of the invasion as “inexplicable”?

options.A: He expressed his frustration with the limits of his knowledge.
options.B: He had a thorough understanding about spider behaviors.
options.C: He believed the invasion was simply a Halloween superstition.
options.D: He showed his excitement of a sudden discovery of the mystery.

questions.stem: Which sentence signifies the transition from a historical mystery to a modern explanation of the spiders’ ability to travel vast distances?

options.A: On October 31, 1832, thousands of tiny red spiders landed from nowhere on his ship, the HMS Beagle.
options.B: This careful assessment of the environment determines the best moment to launch.
options.C: And it really was, until now.
options.D: The starting point for a spider to soar is high up in a tree branch, leaf or fence, where the Earth’s electric field is strongest.

questions.stem: Which of the following pictures can best describe the moment when a spider is about to “balloon”?

options.A: ［圖］蜘蛛站在有葉子的樹枝上，兩隻前腳向上舉起；從腹部末端放出的蛛絲在空中糾纏成一團亂絲。
options.B: ［圖］蜘蛛站在有葉子的樹枝上，腳尖著地、腹部翹起；從腹部末端放出的多條蛛絲呈扇形向上散開、彼此分離不糾纏。
options.C: ［圖］蜘蛛趴在平坦的地面（沙土）上；從腹部末端放出的多條蛛絲呈弧形向上散開，絲線彼此交錯。
options.D: ［圖］蜘蛛趴在平坦的地面（沙土）上；從腹部末端放出幾條細長的波浪狀蛛絲，絲線彼此靠攏、纏在一起向上飄。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Spiders use the electric field to maintain their distance from one another flying in the air.
options.B: The electric field is only active during daylight hours, which makes it easier for spiders to fly.
options.C: A living weather station refers to a spider’s ability to sense the environment and respond to it.
options.D: Spiders generate their own electric field independent of the Earth’s electric field as they fly.
